coachingPoints: Prepare for what the opponent does most, not everything they might do.
Have a Plan B ready for when their best player gets hot.
Keep the pre-game session light: confidence and rhythm over new information.
Write down your first three play calls before tip-off to avoid freezing under pressure.
commonMistakes: Overloading players with too much scouting detail before the game.
Changing the game plan at the last minute and creating confusion.
Practicing too hard the day before the game, leaving legs heavy.
Having no plan for foul trouble or an injury to a key player.
description: How to prepare your team to win — scouting translation, game-plan practices, and pre-game routines that build confidence.
gameSituations: Playoff game against a team built around one dominant scorer.
Back-to-back games with limited recovery time between them.
Rivalry game where emotions run high and discipline is tested.

howTo.detail: Identify the opponent's two or three best players, their main actions, and their weaknesses — and ignore the rest. Scouting everything prepares you for nothing.
howTo.title: Scout with purpose

howTo.detail: Three offensive keys and three defensive keys, written on one page. If the plan does not fit on one page, it is too complicated to execute.
howTo.title: Build a simple game plan

howTo.detail: Dedicate the pre-game practice to rehearsing their actions against your coverages. This is not the time to install new offense — it is the time to rehearse the plan.
howTo.title: Practice the plan

howTo.detail: Know your first substitution pattern and your foul-trouble contingencies before tip-off. Rotations decided calmly beat rotations decided in panic.
howTo.title: Prepare your rotations

howTo.detail: Consistent warm-up timing, consistent messaging, consistent routine. Players feel prepared when the day feels familiar, not rushed.
howTo.title: Set the game-day routine

howTo.detail: Deliver the game plan in five focused minutes. Players remember three points, not fifteen — make each one count.
howTo.title: Communicate the plan clearly

title: Game Preparation
whatIsIt: Game preparation is everything a coach does between games to give the team its best chance: studying the opponent, building a game plan, designing practices that rehearse it, and managing the team's physical and mental state on game day.

Great preparation is specific but simple — three things we must do, three things we must stop. Players play free and confident when the plan is clear; they play tight and confused when it is overloaded.
whyItMatters: Talent wins games, but preparation wins the close ones and the ones you should not win. A well-prepared underdog beats a talented but unprepared favorite regularly. Preparation also reduces anxiety — players who know the plan trust it under pressure.
Consistent preparation also builds program identity. Teams known for being prepared earn a reputation that intimidates opponents before the game even starts.
